repo.description: A library for accelerating Transformer models on NVIDIA GPUs, including using 8-bit and 4-bit floating point (FP8 and FP4) precision on Hopper, Ada and Blackwell GPUs, to provide better performance with lower memory utilization in both training and inference.

detail.body:
# Description

Use the recipe's string representation to select an operation-fusion plan. The previous cache key used the recipe type, backward boundary, and backward override, so a change to another setting on the same recipe type could reuse a plan chosen for the old settings. The new key uses `str(recipe)` and the backward boundary. Recipe classes describe their own settings; `OperationFuser` does not need a growing list of MXFP8, NVFP4, or grouped-MLP recipe options to decide when to re-evaluate fusion.

Recipe representations are cached and invalidated when attributes change. Unexpected public attributes are included too, so changing the dynamically attached `enable_cutedsl_fused_grouped_mlp` flag changes the fusion key. The NVFP4 representation now also includes `disable_rht`.

This follows the motivation in the [original discussion](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3410#discussion_r3856621776).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] Code refactoring

## Changes

- Key the fusion-plan cache by `str(recipe)` and the first operation requiring backward. Keep fusion-plan selection separate from the existing recipe-state reset conditions.
- Cache the module and op-fuser grouped-tensor support checks using the recipe settings each check reads, dtype, split alignment where applicable, and CUDA device. The internal call sites pass the tensor's device, preventing a result from one GPU from being reused for another.
- Cover recipe-representation changes and dynamically attached attributes in the fusion tests.

### CPU overhead of grouped-tensor support checks

BF16 with no recipe on a dlcluster GB200, using `cuda:0` explicitly. Values are median CPU time per call over nine runs of 200,000 calls; the cached path was warm. The uncached functions came from this PR's base commit (`491d557`), and the device-key code is in `793c5ac`.

| Predicate | Before PR (uncached) | After PR (cached) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Module | 1.668 µs | 0.267 µs |
| Op-fuser | 1.549 µs | 0.253 µs |

These numbers use the explicit-device path taken by the internal callers. Omitting `device` requires querying the current CUDA device on each call and has different CPU cost. No GPU kernel changes are included.

### Scope of recipe updates

The fusion-plan cache and quantizer-state reset are separate. This PR changes plan selection; it does not rebuild quantizers when a same-type recipe update changes their configuration. Dynamic recipe update handling is being addressed in [PR #3343](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3343).

# Checklist

- [ ] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [ ] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

inline_comments.body: **Different recipes compare equal** `Recipe.__eq__` now compares strings that leave out meaningful settings. For example, `DelayedScaling(amax_compute_algo='max')` equals `DelayedScaling(amax_compute_algo='most_recent')`. `CustomRecipe` also leaves out `fp8_format`, `fp8_dpa`, and `fp8_mha`. `init_fp8_metadata` uses equality to skip updates, so switching recipes can leave the module using the previous settings. Include all meaningful fields in equality and hashing, and test recipes that differ in these fields.

             self._cached_repr = self._make_repr()
         return self._cached_repr
 
+    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
+        if not isinstance(other, Recipe):
+            return NotImplemented
+        return str(self) == str(other)
+
+    def __hash__(self) -> int:
+        return hash(str(self))

inline_comments.body: **Cache ignores the current GPU** If one process uses GPUs with different capabilities, this cache can return another GPU's support result. A BF16 call on Hopper can cache `True` for `(None, torch.bfloat16)`. The same call on Ampere then returns `True` without checking that GPU and selects an unsupported grouped path. Resolve the current GPU before the cached call and include its identity or capability in the key. The same fix is needed in `is_op_fuser_grouped_tensor_path_supported`. **Knowledge Base Used:** [PyTorch tensor and operator abstractions](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/pytorch-tensors-and-ops.md)

inline_comments.body: **Recipe changes keep old quantizers** The new recipe-change check calls `reset_recipe_state`, but that method does not rebuild quantizers for same-type recipes other than delayed scaling. It only updates the metadata's recipe reference. For example, switching `MXFP8BlockScaling` from E4M3 to HYBRID now changes the fusion plan, but the backward quantizer still emits E4M3 rather than E5M2. Rebuild the affected recipe state and quantizers when these settings change, and test switching recipes on a real quantizing operation. **Knowledge Base Used:** [PyTorch FP8 and low-precision quantization](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/pytorch-quantization.md)

issue_comments.body:
Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; no new blocking issue was found.

Summary

The PR selects fusion plans using the recipe string and the backward boundary. - Fusion plans follow the recipe settings and backward boundary. - Grouped-tensor routing reuses support checks for matching inputs and GPUs. No new actionable issues were found. The previous GPU-cache, grouped-MLP flag, and repeated-settings findings are addressed. `vthumbe1503` explained that refreshing quantizers after same-type recipe changes predates this PR and is deferred to PR #3343; Greptile withdrew that finding. Review checks were based on source inspection; tests were not run.
